findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement StatefulDetectorHandler abstract methods
findings.body: The class inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only has `pass`, so it remains abstract and cannot be instantiated. Any Detector whose `type` slug is 'metric_alert_fire' will trigger `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in models/detector.py, which will raise TypeError when trying to instantiate this handler, breaking metric alert detection. The new abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` must be implemented, or the class must be explicitly marked as abstract and not assigned as a detector_handler.

findings.title: process_detectors silently overwrites duplicate group keys instead of logging
findings.body: The previous code used a set to detect duplicate group keys and logged an error, skipping subsequent duplicates. After changing to a dict, if `handler.evaluate` returns multiple results with the same group key, the later one overwrites the earlier without any log. This can cause loss of evaluation results and hide bugs in detector implementations. Consider logging a warning when overwriting or retaining explicit duplicate detection.

findings.title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`" but the return type is now `dict`. Update the docstring to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Breaking change to process_detectors and evaluate return types
findings.body: Changing the return type of `process_detectors` from `list[tuple[Detector, list[DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` to `list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` and changing the abstract method `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature from returning a list to a dict is a public API break. Any existing callers of `process_detectors` or subclasses of `DetectorHandler` outside this PR will break. Ensure all consumers are updated or provide backwards compatibility.
